title: Krakro
author: Fafa Gilbert
desc: Overripe plantain blended with ginger, cloves and selim grains and deep-fried — no flour at all, and usually eaten with bambara nuts.
longDesc: Krakro is the Akan name and kaklo the Ga one for deep-fried overripe plantain balls, and this Ewe version uses no flour whatsoever: two overripened plantains, twenty grams of ginger, ten cloves, five grains of selim, half a habanero, an onion and a teaspoon of salt, blended and fried in half a litre of oil. The spicing is what distinguishes it — hwentia and cloves are unusual in a fritter — and her note is that it is usually paired with bambara nuts. The method is video-only, so the steps here are reconstructed and labelled as such.
ingredients: 10 cloves — see the note on the ambiguity
steps: // The published method for this recipe is video-only. No written steps exist in the source.
Blend or pound them with the ginger, cloves, selim grains, habanero, onion and salt to a thick batter.
Stir through the coriander and spring onions if using.
Heat the oil for deep frying.
Drop spoonfuls of the batter into the oil.
Fry until deep golden brown all over, turning so they colour evenly.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm with bambara nuts.
// The order above is inferred from the other documented version of this fritter, not from this source.
chefTips: No flour at all in this version, which makes it softer and more intensely of plantain than the versions that add flour and baking powder.
Overripened, not just ripe. Black-skinned plantains are what you want — the sugar is what browns and the softness is what lets it blend.
Grains of selim — hwentia — in a fritter is unusual and it is the signature of this version. Smoky and faintly bitter against the sweet plantain.

Note the ambiguity: the source prints '10 individual cloves', which could mean spice cloves or garlic cloves. Ten spice cloves is a lot but plausible with the selim; ten garlic cloves would dominate. Neither reading is asserted.
Her serving note: usually paired with bambara nuts. The starchy, slightly bitter bean against the sweet fritter is the point.
No fry temperature or time is published in either documented version of this fritter. Medium heat is what the other source advises, to avoid a dark exterior with a raw interior.
The method here is reconstructed from the other documented version. Nothing in the step order is this author's.
commonMistakes: Using merely ripe rather than overripe plantain.
Oil too hot, giving a dark outside and raw middle.
Treating the reconstructed step order as the author's own.
Adding flour, which belongs to the other version.
Leaving out the selim, which is what makes this version distinct.
sources: Quantities from 'Plantain Fritters (Kakro/Krakro)', byline as printed 'Fafa Gilbert', 13 September 2017. Fafa Gilbert is Ewe, from the Volta Region, per her own site — the basis for the community attribution.

Ingredients exactly as printed: 2 overripened plantains; 20g ginger; 10 individual cloves; 5 grains of Selim (Hwentia); ½ habanero chilli; 1 medium onion; 500ml vegetable oil; 1 teaspoon salt. Optional: 10g chopped coriander, 10g spring onions.

AMBIGUITY, flagged and NOT resolved: '10 individual cloves' as printed could mean ten spice cloves or ten garlic cloves. The source does not say. Both readings are noted in the tips and neither is asserted; the ingredient list reproduces the printed wording with a pointer to the note.

METHOD GAP, stated plainly: NO WRITTEN METHOD, NO FRY TEMPERATURE and NO DONENESS CUE exist in the source. The instructions are published as video only. The steps in this entry are explicitly marked as reconstructed from the other documented version of the fritter, and the step list carries a header saying so.
SERVING NOTE, verbatim: 'usually paired with Bambara nuts.'

THE OTHER DOCUMENTED VERSION, which disagrees fundamentally and is the source of the reconstructed method: Sandhya Ramakrishnan, 'Plantain Balls | Kaklo | Krakro', My Cooking Journey, 6 September 2016, updated 29 March 2025, 20 fritters. Its ingredients: 3 overripe plantains; ½ large jalapeno; 3 tablespoons onion; ½ cup all-purpose flour; ½ teaspoon baking powder; ½ teaspoon salt; oil for deep frying. Its method: blend onion and jalapeno with 2-3 tablespoons water, add the plantains, then the dry ingredients, and REST 10-15 MINUTES; fry on medium heat; cook until 'deep brown'. Its warning, which is the useful part: medium heat 'prevents dark exterior with raw interior'. The page says the recipe draws on The Ghana Cookbook. IT IS AN ADAPTATION — jalapeno and baking powder — and the author is not Ghanaian; it is cited for its named byline and its frying warning only.

THE DISAGREEMENT, unreconciled: Gilbert uses NO FLOUR; Ramakrishnan uses ½ cup flour plus baking powder. NEITHER STATES A FRY TEMPERATURE OR TIME. The flour question changes the fritter substantially — flourless is softer and collapses more readily — and neither is corrected toward the other.
ON THE NAMES: krakro is the Akan name and kaklo the Ga name used by some sources, with kakro also appearing. No source consulted sets out which name belongs where, so all are recorded.

NOT FERMENTED: this is a chemically unleavened or flourless batter fried immediately, so it carries no fermentation and needs no cue. Note that the other version's 10-15 minute rest is a hydration rest, not a ferment.
storage: Same day. They go soft and greasy.
reheating: A hot oven briefly. Never the microwave.
healthBenefits: Overripe plantain is high in potassium, vitamin A and vitamin B6.
Ginger and selim both carry documented antimicrobial aromatic compounds.
culturalNote: Fried plantain balls are sold at roadsides all over Ghana and the bambara nut pairing is the detail that makes them a meal rather than a sweet — a handful of the hard, earthy beans alongside the soft sweet fritter. Spicing them with selim and cloves is an Ewe habit and it turns a simple snack into something far more aromatic.
